fields.meta_title: Vendor Survey Builder for Scorecards and Feedback | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a vendor survey from a prompt: quarterly scorecards, vendor feedback, market vendor check-ins, and onboarding. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Vendor Survey to Rate Vendors and Hear From Them
fields.hero_description: Build a vendor survey that scores each vendor or asks vendors about working with you, and saves answers to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Vendor Survey on Emergent Includes
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the vendor survey and the table of answers from one prompt, and another prompt changes either one.
fields.feature_1:
Ratings grouped by what you score

List the areas you score, like on-time delivery and invoice accuracy. Emergent builds 1 to 5 ratings for each area with a comment box under them, and a prompt rewrites any question.
fields.feature_2:
Each answer filed under its vendor

Every response is saved as a row in a database you own, tagged with the vendor and the quarter it covers. Compare a vendor's Q3 scores with Q2 without merging spreadsheets.
fields.feature_3:
Averages checked against your floor

Set a floor, like an average under 3 on any area. On the day the round closes, the app emails the purchasing lead or posts in Slack with that vendor's scores and comments.
fields.feature_4:
Vendor lists pulled from your books

The app can read your vendor list from QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite through their APIs. Surveys go to vendors you still buy from, and each score lines up with its account.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Market vendors and drivers answer one question per screen on a phone. Emergent sets no response caps on surveys: 60 vendors or 600 can answer, and each reply lands in one table.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code on paid plans

Host the survey on your own domain, which Emergent includes and which uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it in your stack.

fields.tab_content_1:
Ludlow Box scores 2.5 on on-time delivery

Hartsfield Bakery runs 6 stores, and each quarter every store manager rates the vendors from 1 to 5 on on-time delivery, order accuracy, quality, and invoices. In Q3, Ludlow Box averaged 2.5 on on-time delivery, under the floor of 3. The app emailed the purchasing lead, Elspeth Wyndell, who booked a review call.
fields.tab_content_2:
When 19 of 31 vendors name late payments

Once a year, Copperleaf Co-op asks its 52 local vendors how ordering, payment timing, and shelf placement work for them, and saves answers without vendor names. This year 31 answered, and 19 said payments arrived late. The co-op moved its vendor payment run from monthly to every 2 weeks.
fields.tab_content_3:
After 22 vendors ask, closing moves to 2 pm

Bexley Wharf Market sends its 64 vendors an end-of-season survey with one question per screen, answered at the stall on a phone. Of the 64, 48 answered, with 41 planning to return. Asked what to change, 22 wanted a later close than 1 pm, and the manager, Imogen Strand, moved next season's closing time to 2 pm.
fields.tab_content_4:
A 21-day lead time waits for procurement

Ravensby Hotels sends each prospective vendor a 12-question onboarding questionnaire: lead time, minimum order, and which of its 3 hotels it delivers to. A lead time over 14 days sends the answers to the procurement manager, Cass Delacroix. Beaumont Linen answered 21 days, and its first order waits for her review.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Vendor Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a vendor survey that rates what each vendor controls and ends with one agreed fix per low score.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide which way the survey points
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Rate only what the vendor controls
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about one thing per statement
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Reuse the same wording each round
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide first whether your team rates the vendor or the vendor rates working with you. A scorecard goes to the people who receive the orders, and a feedback survey goes to each vendor's account contact. Put the direction in your prompt, and Emergent builds the survey around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick 4 or 5 areas, each with 2 or 3 statements. York University's procurement office reviews areas such as quality of delivery, invoicing accuracy, and adherence to scope of work. Leave out anything your own team causes, like a purchase order sent late.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Split any statement that covers two things, like delivery speed and packaging. Pew Research Center notes that questions asking respondents to evaluate more than one concept are difficult for respondents to answer. Under each area, add one open question on what would raise the score.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Use the same statements and the same 1 to 5 scale every quarter. Pew Research Center advises that when measuring change over time, it is important to use the same question wording. Put any new question at the end, where it changes nothing above it.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the floor before the first round
fields.howto_step_5_des: Agree on the score that starts a review, like any area averaging below 3, and who hears about it. Name one owner per vendor category, like the purchasing lead for packaging. Put both in the prompt, and the alert is part of the build.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test with a manager and a vendor
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before the first send, have one store manager and one friendly vendor answer for real. Pew Research Center calls pretesting an essential step in the questionnaire design process. Fix any statement either one misread, and check that each answer lands under the right vendor.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share the scores and agree on one fix
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send each vendor its own scores and the comments that explain them, without the names of the people who wrote them. Agree on one fix per low area with a date, then check whether the score moves in the next round.

faq_plan.a: A vendor survey is a questionnaire about the companies a business buys from. Either staff rate a vendor on delivery and invoices, or the vendors say how working with the business goes. York University's procurement office describes its online Vendor Evaluation Survey form as the tool used by a unit or department when evaluating a vendor.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a vendor survey?
faq_plan.a: Tell Emergent's AI survey builder what to rate and who should hear about a low score. Emergent builds the survey and its database from that prompt, and you edit any question by prompting. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What vendor survey questions should I ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask what a respondent can judge from their own orders. For a scorecard: How often did deliveries arrive on the promised date? How accurate were this quarter's invoices? How fast was a problem fixed? For vendor feedback: Are purchase orders clear? Do payments arrive when promised? Close either one with an open question on what to change.

faq_plan.q: Is there a vendor survey template I can start from?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent writes one from a prompt that names your vendors and what to rate, with a group of rating statements for each area. Change a few sections, and the same template turns into questions for the vendors themselves. Asking customers what they would pay is a different job, and a pricing survey covers it.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a vendor survey have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it under 20: 4 or 5 areas with 2 or 3 rating statements each, plus one open question per area. Time the set before you send it: a store manager who rates 6 vendors answers it 6 times in one sitting.

faq_plan.q: How often should I send a vendor survey?
faq_plan.a: Quarterly works for vendors you order from weekly, since each round covers enough deliveries to judge. Once a year fits vendors you use a few times a year, and a feedback survey sent to vendors. Keep the same months each year. On Emergent, each round's answers land in a database you own, next to the round before.

faq_plan.q: What should a vendor satisfaction survey ask vendors?
faq_plan.a: Ask how easy you are to sell to: clear purchase orders, payment on the agreed date, and quick answers. It works like a customer satisfaction survey pointed at the companies that sell to you. Harvard's Government Performance Lab tells government buyers that hearing from current and prospective vendors can provide valuable feedback on your procurement process.

faq_plan.q: Should vendor survey answers be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: For feedback from vendors, yes: save answers without the vendor's name and say so in the invitation. For a scorecard, keep the vendor's name, because the point is to score that vendor, but leave out which manager wrote each rating. Then a vendor who reads its comments cannot tell which store sent them.

faq_plan.q: What rating scale works best in a vendor survey?
faq_plan.a: A 1 to 5 scale with every point labeled, from Poor to Excellent, used on every statement. One scale lets averages compare across areas and quarters. Add a Not applicable option. A manager who never handles invoices then skips that statement instead of guessing a 3.

faq_plan.q: Can one vendor survey go to customers too?
faq_plan.a: Keep them apart. Vendors and customers answer about different relationships, and one shared table blurs every average. Send vendors this survey and send buyers a customer feedback survey. Emergent puts no cap on how many vendors or buyers answer either one.

plan.angle: The SERP for vendor survey is template galleries and a few procurement pages: a list of rating questions for one direction, usually scoring a vendor. Searchers mean two directions: a team rating its vendors, and a business asking its vendors how working with it goes. This page builds both and shows four built surveys that each end in a decision: a bakery's quarterly scorecard that emails purchasing when a score falls under 3.0, a co-op's yearly vendor feedback that moved its payment run, a farmers market's end-of-season vendor check-in answered on phones, and a hotel group's onboarding questionnaire that holds a 21-day lead time for procurement. The FAQ answers what a builder asks: which questions, a template, length, scale, frequency, sharing scores, anonymity and keeping vendor and customer surveys apart.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Vendor Survey to Rate Vendors and Hear From Them' covers both directions; hero 'Build a vendor survey that scores each vendor or asks vendors about working with you, and saves answers to a database you own.' (125 chars); how-to description one sentence with the primary.

intent.evidence: Delivers questions (FAQ 3 lists scorecard and feedback questions), a template answer (FAQ 4), length, frequency, scale and anonymity, plus a 7-step how-to; covers both senses (rating vendors, vendors rating you).

specificity.evidence: Procurement vocabulary: 'on-time delivery and invoice accuracy', 'purchase order sent late', 'payment run', 'lead time over 14 days'.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on verbs or full sentences: 'List the areas you score', 'Every response is saved as a row', 'Set a floor'.

craft.evidence: No blocking craft issues; notes on FAQ 6 broken clause and FAQ 5 count.

voice.evidence: 'Ludlow Box averaged 2.5 on on-time delivery, under the floor of 3'; '19 said payments arrived late'; plain verbs throughout.

truth.evidence: York University used only as an attributed example (step 2 'York University's procurement office reviews areas such as...'; FAQ 1 'York University's procurement office describes its online Vendor Evaluation Survey form as...'), never as a general or regulatory rule; Pew sentences (steps 3, 4, 6) and Harvard GPL (FAQ 7, 'tells government buyers') inside their quoted spans. Emergent claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, conversational, api-connect (QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite), no-caps, custom-domain, code-export, free-start.

distinct.evidence: No sibling primary in headings; customer satisfaction survey, customer feedback survey and pricing survey only as FAQ link anchors; hotel onboarding tab does not headline vendor application or vendor management workflow.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic builder questions, answer-first; hub link in item 2; secondaries vendor survey questions (3), vendor survey template (4). PAA gate 10 pass, 0 reject, 0 flag.
